reader.requirement: At --std 85 every alphanumeric function (CHAR, CURRENT-DATE, LOWER-CASE, REVERSE, UPPER-CASE, WHEN-COMPILED) is an elementary item of class and category alphanumeric, of the size its definition states, with implicit usage DISPLAY: it moves, compares, strings and class-tests as an alphanumeric DISPLAY item and is refused as an arithmetic operand and as a receiving operand.

edition-consulted.switches: D8 window: IntroducedIn 85 against DialectLevel for each function
numeric-function-identifier-operand-2002 is asked only for a NUMERIC category; an alphanumeric function passes as an identifier at every edition

reader.edition-search: CategoryOf/ImplicitUsageOf and IntrinsicResultLength take no edition; grep of IntrinsicCatalog.cs for Edition/Version found none
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_f13_05 covers REVERSE and UPPER-CASE size, moves and class tests; not CHAR/CURRENT-DATE/WHEN-COMPILED sizes, a STRING sender or INSPECT operand, comparisons, or the arithmetic- and receiving-operand refusals

probes.printed: L-CHAR=01 L-CDATE=21 L-WC=21 L-LOWER=07 L-UPPER-ODO3=03 L-UPPER-ODO5=05 L-REV-REFMOD=03 STR=[12ABCDEFGA] P=11 CMP-NUM=EQ CMP-ALNUM=GT CMP-CHAR=EQ INSP-CNT=02
probes.expected: sizes 1/21/21/argument length (ODO group at its current length); STRING admits them as DISPLAY senders; nonnumeric comparison with a numeric integer item; INSPECT TALLYING FOR ALL FUNCTION CHAR (66)

probes.printed: COBOL0844 FUNCTION REVERSE is not a numeric operand (COMPUTE and ADD); COBOL1632 INSPECT REPLACING into a function-identifier is a receiving operand
probes.expected: an alphanumeric function is no arithmetic operand and never a receiving operand (§1989:A.2.3)

citations.check: OK  §1989:A.2.3 GR1  (2.3 TYPES OF FUNCTIONS)  the text is in GR1

reader.notes: IntrinsicSig.CategoryOf maps type Alphanumeric to category alphanumeric and ImplicitUsageOf gives it usage Display in one place; IntrinsicResultLength carries the fixed or argument-1 size. MOVE 'AB' TO FUNCTION REVERSE (W2) is refused as a parse error (COBOL5506), a correct refusal with a generic message.

refuter.evidence: xgr1.cob at --std 85 exercises the category-alphanumeric moves and the implicit DISPLAY usage the reader did not: MOVE FUNCTION REVERSE (D) TO PIC 9(3) = 321, TO PIC ZZ9 = [321], UPPER-CASE TO PIC A(3) = [ABC], TO PIC X/X = [A/B]; INSPECT FUNCTION UPPER-CASE (X) TALLYING CNT FOR ALL "B" CHARACTERS BEFORE "2" = 03 (the inspected item must be usage DISPLAY, §1985 INSPECT SR1); UNSTRING FUNCTION UPPER-CASE (X) DELIMITED BY "1" = [A ][B2]; class tests NUMERIC and ALPHABETIC-UPPER true; EVALUATE subject; comparison with the integer literal 321 EQ and with ALL "A" EQ. xgr2/xgr2b: STRING ... INTO FUNCTION REVERSE (X), ACCEPT FUNCTION UPPER-CASE (X), INITIALIZE FUNCTION REVERSE (X) are refused (COBOL5506 parse errors: correct refusal, generic text), and FUNCTION CHAR (50) as a subscript is refused COBOL0844 + COBOL0900. cite.py: OK  §1989:A.2.3 GR1  (2.3 TYPES OF FUNCTIONS)  the text is in GR1; OK  §1985:IV.4.3.8.3.3 SR3  (4.3.8.3.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR3. No edition switch on the category or usage of an alphanumeric function was found beyond the reader's two sites.
